design: Arms INTERLEAVED U,P,U,P... rather than sequential, because both benches' levers faded across the session and two arms run one after the other are not comparable. Burners started inside the same script as the arms, with trap cleanup EXIT INT TERM so an interruption cannot leave load or a patched server.py behind.
not_claimed: That promotion does not help. Two floor-effect nulls are not evidence about a mechanism.

That the fade is a real effect rather than this project's fourth look-alike. #48's incidence drift had the same shape and dissolved four separate times, once into my own miscount of the unit of independence.
so: The promotion hypothesis is untestable on this bench in its current state, and now demonstrated so at the load linux-x1's sweep says is sufficient. windows-desk reached the same position independently - their promoted and unpromoted arms both came back 0/10.

the_lever_has_gone.means: The contention lever faded to undetectable on this bench over about 3.5 hours, and DOUBLING the load did not recover it. That is stronger than the 1x series alone: 2x should have more than compensated for a fade and did not.

the_load_was_really_on: Per-run wall time is the load witness and it reads a clean ladder on this bench: unloaded 10.5-11.0 s, 1x 11.4-11.8 s, 2x 12.2-12.6 s. This run sat at 12.2-12.6 throughout, so the null is not another arm whose load had stopped - that failure happened three times today and is what the witness exists for.
verdict: INCONCLUSIVE again - the baseline did not fire even at 2x
